detail: PubMed-only searching missed a randomised trial (C12), an adequately powered trial (C13), two sildenafil sources (C14), a phase 2b null (C15) and a registry-only harm result (C23). Eleven of the twelve Phase 4 corrections are retrieval artefacts of the Phase 2 search, not changes of judgement about the same evidence.
The registry-results check was run for the 22 candidate subjects, not for all 281 landscape entities (action A5).
Two candidate key results could not be verified against primary full text (P10, P17) and are recorded as held, not rejected and not promoted.
No pooling or re-estimation was performed in Phase 4; all figures are quoted from their source reports.

scope: one source with an internal inconsistency
detail: The endurance-time interval in PMID 37012071 as printed does not contain its own point estimate; reproduced verbatim and flagged, full text not obtained.

scope: Phase 2 search strategy; Phase 6 action A5
detail: Entity-level literature searching in Phase 2 was PubMed-only and did not include a registry posted-results check, so trials that were completed but unpublished were graded as absent evidence. Action A5 corrected this for the whole landscape, but two consequences remain: (i) nine entities now rest on registry postings whose between-arm analyses the sponsor never posted, which can be described and not weighed; (ii) the sweep covers ClinicalTrials.gov only - EudraCT, jRCT, ChiCTR and other national registries were not swept, so the same class of miss may persist for trials registered elsewhere.

scope: Phase 2 traditional-medicine screen; Phase 6 action A4
detail: The record's coverage of traditional Chinese medicine rests on English-indexed sources. Direct access to CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed, ChiCTR and the WHO ICTRP portal was not achieved from this environment (ICTRP's gateway refuses non-browser clients; ChiCTR's search requires an encrypted browser session; the Chinese bibliographic databases are subscription-gated). Action A4 quantified the resulting gap from secondary reviews: at least 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections and several further pools totalling thousands of participants sit outside the record, and no injection product appears in the landscape. Any statement this record makes about traditional Chinese medicine in IPF is therefore made on a demonstrably partial sample, and the direction of the missing evidence is unknown.
